A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the number of vertices with degree $k$, in the case where $k\geq 1$, converges in distribution to the Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda=\frac{\alpha^k}{k}$, where $\alpha$ is the mean degree of the graph.
the distribution of the number of nodes of a given degree can be approximated by a Poisson distribution with a certain parameter.

the distribution of the number of nodes of a certain degree in random graphs converges to the Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda = \frac{n}{2}\sum_{i=0}^k (-1)^i\binom{k}{i}\frac{p^i(1-p)^{k-i}}{i!}$ where $p$ and $k$ are the probability of an edge between two vertices and the degree of a given vertex, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymptotic distribution of the number of edges in a random graph is a Poisson distribution.
the number of vertices with a given degree in the random graph is asymptotically Poisson distributed with the parameter being the probability of an edge.

in the general case, the number of vertices with a given degree is asymptotically Poisson distributed with parameter equal to the product of the probability of an edge and the probability of a vertex of the corresponding degree.
